outcome: need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusions
cohort: The study included 420 patients (mothers and their neonates) from the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology Unit-2, Civil Hospital, Karachi, evenly divided between early and delayed cord clamping groups.
finding: Delayed umbilical cord clamping (DCC) was found to be safe and feasible, leading to fewer infants requiring red blood cell transfusions and improving several important hematological parameters for newborns compared to early cord clamping.
